title: Bernard Shaw and Churchill: The Opening Night Tickets
summary: Shaw sent Churchill two premiere tickets: 'Bring a friend, if you have one.' Churchill replied: 'Cannot attend first night; will attend second night, if there is one!'
keywords: Bernard Shaw and Churchill: The Opening Night Tickets
full_text:
In early twentieth-century Britain, two towering masters of the English language sparred with dazzling wit: Nobel Prize-winning dramatist George Bernard Shaw and statesman Winston Churchill.

Preparing to premiere a new play in the West End, Shaw decided to test Churchill's composure. He mailed Churchill two complimentary tickets accompanied by a brief note:

**"My dear Churchill,
Enclosed are two tickets to the opening night of my new play.
Bring a friend... if you have one!
Yours, G. B. Shaw."**

The insinuation was clear: that Churchill was an abrasive, friendless politician!

Churchill received the letter, grinned broadly, and immediately dictated a return telegram:

**"My dear Shaw,
Cannot possibly attend first night; am too busy.
Will attend second night... if there is one!
Yours, Winston Churchill."**

The counter-punch was devastating: Churchill implied that Shaw's play was so dreadful that it would close after opening night!

Their verbal fencing remains an immortal classic of literary banter.
moral: Refined wit and intellectual fencing between titans demonstrate how humor can celebrate genius without breeding malice.

authenticity_note: A celebrated staple of British 20th-century wit. While widely circulated in popular anthologies and attributed to Shaw and Churchill, Churchill scholars (including the Churchill Project) classify it as popular folklore/apocrypha rather than a verified archival exchange.
